approaches.name: Iliofemoral (Smith-Petersen) approach to the hip (periprosthetic)
approaches.corridor: Anterior iliofemoral exposure developing the interval between tensor fasciae latae and sartorius superficially and releasing rectus femoris to reach the anterior hip and ilium

procedure_applications.condition: Direct anterior access to the hip and ilium is needed, though it is uncommon for periprosthetic acetabular fractures

positioning.text: Position supine with the limb free for rotation and traction and a bump under the ipsilateral pelvis.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the lateral iliac crest and the anterior superior iliac spine.

incision.text: Begin the incision over the lateral iliac crest, follow it to the ASIS, then turn distally along the lateral border of the sartorius toward the patella.

superficial_interval.text: Develop the interval between the tensor fasciae latae and the sartorius, protecting the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve near the ASIS.

deep_interval.text: Identify, divide, and ligate the lateral femoral circumflex vessels distally, and release the direct head of rectus femoris from the anterior inferior iliac spine, taking the reflected head for more proximal exposure.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue with the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve, the tensor fasciae latae and sartorius interval, rectus femoris, the lateral femoral circumflex vessels, and the anterior hip capsule and ilium.

structures_at_risk.text: The lateral femoral cutaneous nerve near the ASIS and the lateral femoral circumflex vessels are at risk.

danger_zones.text: The region just medial and distal to the ASIS is the danger zone for the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve.

retraction_hazards.text: Avoid vigorous medial retraction near the sartorius that stretches the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve.

exposure.text: Provides the most direct access to the anterior hip and the outer and inner tables of the ilium.

limitations.text: It gives poor access to the posterior column and is not commonly used for periprosthetic acetabular fractures.

indications.text: Indicated when direct anterior access to the hip and ilium is required, and it can be extended along the iliac crest.

closure.text: Repair the capsule, reattach the rectus femoris if released, repair the abductor origin, and close in layers over a subfascial drain.

complications.text: Complications include lateral femoral cutaneous nerve injury, hematoma from the circumflex vessels, and heterotopic ossification.

questions.question: Along which muscle border does the Smith-Petersen incision turn distally?
questions.answer: Along the lateral border of the sartorius.

questions.question: Which vessels are ligated in the deep dissection?
Which nerve is most at risk near the ASIS?

approaches.name: Kocher-Langenbeck approach to the acetabulum (periprosthetic)
approaches.corridor: Posterior approach splitting gluteus maximus and detaching the short external rotators to expose the posterior column and retroacetabular surface, protecting the sciatic nerve

sources.title: Kocher-Langenbeck approach to the acetabulum (periprosthetic hip)

procedure_applications.condition: A periprosthetic acetabular or posterior column fracture needs posterior exposure
A posterior wall or column acetabular fracture is fixed

positioning.text: Position prone or lateral, with the lateral position preferred for periprosthetic fracture and revision arthroplasty.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the posterior superior iliac spine, the greater trochanter, and the femoral shaft.

incision.text: Begin several centimeters distal and lateral to the PSIS, run anteriorly over the greater trochanter, and curve distally along the lateral femoral shaft to the mid-thigh.

superficial_interval.text: Split the gluteus maximus along its fibers from the trochanter proximally to the first neurovascular bundle, optionally releasing its femoral insertion 1 cm from the gluteal tuberosity.

deep_interval.text: Tag the piriformis and conjoined obturator internus and gemelli with heavy nonabsorbable stay sutures and detach them to expose the posterior capsule and retroacetabular surface.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, fascia lata, gluteus maximus, the short external rotators, and the posterior column and capsule.

structures_at_risk.text: The sciatic nerve behind the short external rotators is the principal structure at risk throughout the exposure.

danger_zones.text: The retroacetabular surface and the greater and lesser sciatic notches are danger zones for the sciatic nerve.

retraction_hazards.text: Maintain knee flexion at about 90 degrees and hip extension to reduce sciatic nerve tension during retraction.

exposure.text: Exposes the posterior column, retroacetabular surface, and the greater and lesser sciatic notches.

limitations.text: Anterior column and wall access is limited, so complex anterior involvement may require an additional or different approach.

indications.text: Indicated for ORIF of periprosthetic acetabular and femoral fractures and for revision arthroplasty.

closure.text: Repair the capsular flap and reattach the external rotator tendons through drill holes in the greater trochanter, then close in layers.

complications.text: Complications include sciatic nerve injury, posterior instability, heterotopic ossification, and wound problems.

questions.question: What knee and hip position reduces sciatic nerve tension in the Kocher-Langenbeck approach?
questions.answer: Knee flexion at about 90 degrees with hip extension.

questions.question: Which acetabular surfaces does this approach expose?
questions.answer: The posterior column and retroacetabular surface, with access to the sciatic notches.

questions.question: How are the external rotators managed for later repair?
questions.answer: They are tagged with heavy nonabsorbable stay sutures before detachment.

approaches.name: Anterolateral (Watson-Jones) approach to the hip (periprosthetic)
approaches.corridor: Anterolateral interval between tensor fasciae latae and gluteus medius, releasing anterior vastus lateralis to reach the anterior hip capsule and femoral neck

sources.title: Direct lateral approach to the proximal femur (periprosthetic hip)

procedure_applications.condition: A proximal periprosthetic femoral fracture is exposed through an anterolateral interval

positioning.text: Position supine or lateral with the greater trochanter and proximal femur accessible.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the lateral greater trochanter and the iliac crest tubercle.

incision.text: Start a slightly anteriorly curved incision about 7 to 10 cm proximal to the lateral greater trochanter and extend it about 10 cm distal to the trochanter.

superficial_interval.text: Incise the fascia lata and develop the interval between the gluteus medius and the tensor fasciae latae, ligating or cauterizing the vessels crossing it.

deep_interval.text: Retract the tensor fasciae latae anteriorly and gluteus medius posteriorly, release vastus lateralis from the anterior inferior trochanteric region, and open a T-shaped capsulotomy with anterior and posterior stay sutures.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, fascia lata, the tensor fasciae latae and gluteus medius interval, vastus lateralis, and the anterior hip capsule.

structures_at_risk.text: The superior gluteal nerve, which crosses about 3 to 5 cm proximal to the greater trochanter, limits proximal dissection between the medius and tensor fasciae latae.

danger_zones.text: Proximal dissection more than 3 to 5 cm above the trochanter between medius and tensor fasciae latae is the danger zone for the superior gluteal nerve.

retraction_hazards.text: Avoid excessive proximal retraction of the gluteus medius that endangers the superior gluteal nerve.

exposure.text: Exposes the anterior hip capsule, femoral head, and neck, though access to the joint is somewhat limited.

limitations.text: The approach gives somewhat limited access to the hip joint and less distal femoral exposure than the direct lateral approach.

indications.text: Indicated for open reduction of proximal periprosthetic femoral fractures and for revision arthroplasty.

closure.text: Repair the capsule, reattach vastus lateralis, and close the fascia lata in layers.

complications.text: Complications include superior gluteal nerve injury with abductor weakness, periarticular ossification, and hematoma.

questions.question: Which interval defines the Watson-Jones approach?
questions.answer: Between the gluteus medius and the tensor fasciae latae.

questions.question: Which nerve limits proximal dissection in this interval?
questions.answer: The superior gluteal nerve, about 3 to 5 cm above the greater trochanter.

questions.question: What is a noted limitation of the anterolateral approach?
questions.answer: Somewhat limited access to the hip joint.
